title: By the Time the Report Arrives
author: Eddie Killian
summary: Eddie Killian argues that some organizational problems do not merely grow between reporting periods, they reproduce there. Starting from a repeat-repair example in maintenance, he shows how a closed work order records that someone acted without recording that the asset was restored. He uses the chessboard-and-rice story as a model of accumulation, in which each unresolved failure becomes the starting position for the next one. The essay then names two clocks, the operating clock and the executive clock, and warns that a company can honor every reporting deadline while losing control of the work. He extends the same logic to onboarding and to upward reporting, where shortcuts spread through informal training and softened bad news weakens decisions. His practical conclusion is that operating reviews should ask what is reproducing, what carries it forward, and where the signal is delayed or altered.
points: A closed ticket proves that someone acted, not that the underlying failure was resolved, so repeat repairs can be one continuous story told as separate jobs.
Leaders live on an executive clock that is slower than the operating clock, which means a monthly number can describe a past the organization has already moved beyond.
Poor onboarding does not leave a new hire unformed; it hands the training to the informal organization, which transmits shortcuts and silent exceptions.
Softened reports compound: each diluted message produces a weaker decision and a harder next problem, so leaders are separated from events by a chain of reporting choices.
Better operating reviews ask what is reproducing and how quickly, not only what last month's number was.
quotes: A closed work order says that someone acted. It does not say that the asset was restored to a known condition.
The report did not miss the problem. It arrived after the problem had already reproduced.
Every organization runs on two clocks. One is the operating clock: the time required for a defect, workaround, assumption, or customer commitment to create its next exposure.
Poor onboarding does not leave a person unformed. It allows the informal organization to conduct the training.
When the issue finally becomes visible, leaders may describe themselves as surprised. They were not surprised by one event. They were separated from it by a chain of reporting choices.

Information can arrive quickly and still be useless if it loses meaning on the way upward. A report is early warning only when it arrives before the fact it describes has had time to reproduce, and when it preserves enough of that fact for someone to act.
The warning sign is not recurrence alone. It is recurrence without an understood cause, accepted failure mode, owner, and decision.
